co_poudre_canyon.blurb: Poudre Canyon runs northwest out of Fort Collins, with crags strung along the valley from its mouth upstream. Bouldering and sport climbing are about equally common, trad makes up a solid third, and there are a few ice lines. Sport leads cluster between 5.10 and 5.12 with fewer easy ones, while boulder problems stretch from V0 to roughly V10 with the bulk in the middle grades. Granite is the rock at Greyrock, which offers bolted slabs of one to three pitches and longer crack routes on its southeast side. The small crags near the canyon mouth are short, quick to reach and can be climbed through the whole year. Larger areas include West of Rustic, The Narrows, The Palace and Greyrock.

or_smith_rock.blurb: Smith Rock rises above the Crooked River in the high desert of central Oregon, close to Redmond and Terrebonne. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, with a large trad contingent and a modest amount of bouldering. Grades are centred on 5.10 to 5.12, with a healthy number of 5.13s and a handful of harder lines above them. Most of the main cliffs are welded tuff, while the upper and lower gorge are basalt, where the climbing leans toward balance and cracks. Red Wall is tinted red to purple by iron in the rock. Summer afternoons are fiercely hot and climbers chase shade, whereas winter brings freezing temperatures and thinner crowds. Big sectors include The Marsupials, the Lower Gorge, the Monument Area and Christian Brothers.

ca_san_jacinto_mountains.blurb: The San Jacinto Mountains stand south of Interstate 10 near Palm Springs, with Idyllwild as the main mountain town. This is overwhelmingly a bouldering range, with only a small amount of roped trad, sport and top-rope climbing. The rock is granite, ranging from smooth and friendly to rough enough to chew up skin. Problems run from the very easy to V8 in good numbers, with a thin tail of harder ones. Most of the range sits above 6,000 feet, so it is mainly a spring-through-fall destination. At Black Mountain, around 7,000 feet among pines, talus and ridges, spring and autumn are the most comfortable times. The biggest areas are The Tramway, Black Mountain, Backcountry Bouldering and Idyllwild County Park.

mt_northwest_region.blurb: Northwest Montana spreads from the Kalispell and Flathead country through the Missoula valleys and over to Glacier National Park. Sport and trad climbing share most of the routes, backed by a good amount of bouldering plus some winter ice up to WI5. Grades are mostly 5.8 to 5.12, with moderates well covered. The rock changes from place to place: extremely hard quartzite with sharp edges and thin cracks near Lake Koocanusa, argillite on rolling ridges north of Whitefish, and granite and limestone elsewhere. Many crags are scattered and low-key, linked by dirt roads rather than clustered in one valley. Larger areas include the Kalispell Area, Lost Horse, Kootenai Canyon and the Missoula Area.

ab_bow_valley.blurb: The Bow Valley stretches through Canmore, Banff and Lake Louise in the Alberta Rockies. Sport climbing dominates, with bolted limestone crags in nearly every side valley, plus long trad lines on the big walls above and a fair amount of winter mixed and ice. Grades run mostly from 5.10 to 5.13, and the steep hard-route cliffs reach well beyond that, though easier routes exist for newcomers. The rock season is fairly short, usually April through October, while ice climbing can start as early as October and last into April. Quieter crags offer relief when the popular ones are busy. Key areas include Cougar Canyon, Echo Canyon, Heart Creek and Acéphale.

nc_3_piedmont_region.blurb: The Piedmont gathers the climbing between the Triangle and the mountains around Boone, most of it within reach of Winston-Salem and Charlotte. Bouldering and trad lead, followed by sport and top-rope, with ice only at one spot. Most routes sit between 5.7 and 5.12, and boulder problems are mainly easy to moderate. Moore's Wall at Hanging Rock is the standout, with quartzite offering steep adventurous trad, very hard sport lines and plenty of boulders. Crowders Mountain mixes boulders and trad with some sport and top-rope, while Pilot Mountain leans toward sport and top-rope. Because these areas sit close to big cities, expect them to be busy on weekends.
